subject.title: chore(deps): bump the actions group across 1 directory with 14 updates

question: After the three pin-guard mismatches are repaired, should OpenClaw accept this grouped set of third-party action revisions across token, publishing, scanning, and Codex permission boundaries?
rationale: The revisions execute external code with privileged credentials and security permissions, and repository ownership explicitly assigns the central guard surface to secops; automation cannot make the final trust decision.

options.title: Repair and approve group
options.body: Update the three stale assertions, verify the exact upstream revisions and permissions, and accept the group after focused checks pass.

options.title: Split privileged actions
options.body: Land routine setup-action updates separately from token-minting, publishing, CodeQL, and Codex-agent revisions to reduce review scope.

options.title: Retain current pins
options.body: Keep the existing revisions until secops has enough provenance and compatibility evidence for the grouped upgrade.

recommendation.title: Repair and approve group
recommendation.body: Update the three stale assertions, verify the exact upstream revisions and permissions, and accept the group after focused checks pass.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the secops ownership boundary and recent CodeQL workflow changes covering the most security-sensitive paths in this group.
